name: 2 Samuel

facts.author: The author is not named. Jewish tradition holds that the prophets Nathan and Gad completed the story begun by Samuel, since 1 and 2 Samuel were once one book.
facts.audience: The people of Israel, to show God's covenant with David and the cost of sin

about: 2 Samuel tells the story of David's forty years as king. After mourning Saul and Jonathan, David reigns over Judah at Hebron for seven and a half years, and then over all Israel (5:4-5). He takes Jerusalem and makes it his capital, brings the ark of God there with great joy, and defeats Israel's enemies.

When David wants to build a house for God, the Lord promises instead to build a house for David: a son will build the temple, and David's throne and kingdom will last for ever (7:12-16). This promise points to Jesus Christ, the Son of David.

Then David falls into sin with Bathsheba and has her husband Uriah killed. When Nathan the prophet faces him, David confesses, and God forgives him (12:13), but trouble follows in his family. His son Amnon wrongs Tamar, Absalom kills Amnon and later rebels against his father, and David weeps for Absalom when he dies. The book closes with David's songs of praise and an altar built on the threshing floor of Araunah.

themes.title: God's covenant with David
themes.text: God promises David a house, a kingdom and a throne for ever, fulfilled in Christ.

themes.title: Sin, confession and forgiveness
themes.text: David's great sin is forgiven when he confesses it, yet its painful results remain in his family.

themes.title: A king after God's heart
themes.text: With all his failures David loves the Lord, seeks Him, worships Him and turns back to Him.

themes.title: God's perfect way
themes.text: David praises God as his rock and shield, whose way is perfect and whose word is true (22:31).
